Paddock

Three modules in the spirit of Peter Blasser's coupled analog circuits: Swerve (a bounce generator), Gallop (four bounce oscillators that bound each other) and Tumble (five touch-coupled rhythm cores with gongs). Version 2.0.0, Hær.

The idea: a horse

All three are built on one simple circuit. A voltage rises at one speed until it reaches an upper bound, turns, falls at another speed to a lower bound, and turns again. That makes a triangle. The trick is that the bounds are inputs: move them and the pitch follows the gap (half the gap, twice the pitch). If the lower bound rises above the upper one, the circuit fights itself and throws the voltage back and forth across the overlap, faster the deeper the overlap. That is the paradox sound.

Every module is one "unit": a saved seed gives it its own small part tolerances and slow drift, so two Gallops never behave identically. Right-click for Character (Clean, Factory, Worn) and New unit (re-roll the tolerances).

Swerve (12 HP)

ControlWhat it does
UP / DOWNSpeed of the rise and of the fall. Equal = triangle; one fast = ramp or saw; both together set pitch.
HIGH / LOWThe bounds, −5 to +5 V, added to the HIGH and LOW jacks. Closer together = faster and smaller.
RANGECV (0.005 to 20 Hz), LOW (0.5 to 128 Hz), AUDIO (16 Hz to 8 kHz). Pitch is marked for bounds at ±5 V.
MODECYCLE runs freely. ONCE waits at LOW; a ▲ TRIG makes one rise and fall, so it works as an envelope with separate attack (UP) and release (DOWN).
UP CV, BOTH CV, DOWN CV1 V/oct at full, with attenuverters. BOTH is the pitch input.
▲ TRIG / ▼ TRIGTurn it upwards or downwards right now (resets the shape mid-flight).
TRI, SQR, TOP, BTMPosition; direction (+5 V rising); 10 ms pulses when it turns at the top and at the bottom.
DIR lightGreen rising, red falling; the small yellow light shows paradox.

Gallop (24 HP)

Four horses stacked: horse 1 bounces between +RAIL and horse 2, horse 2 between horse 1 and horse 3, horse 3 between horse 2 and horse 4, horse 4 between horse 3 and −RAIL. Every horse pushes on its neighbours, so the four shapes keep changing each other.

ControlWhat it does
RATEEach horse's speed (pitch in AUDIO range; marked for a horse with a quarter of the stack).
TILTCentre = equal rise and fall. Left: slow rise, fast fall. Right: the reverse.
CV + INPer horse: moves rate (1 V/oct at full) and tilt a little, like the original's control input.
HIGH / LOW jacksBound inserts. Patch one to replace that horse's neighbour (or the rail) with your own voltage.
TRI / SQREach horse's position and direction.
RANGE, RAILShared range switch; RAIL sets the top and bottom of the stack (1 to 8 V), so the output level.
FM + V/OCTPitch for all four together.
PARADOX lightsRed when that horse's bounds have crossed.
MIX, POLYAll four summed; or all four on one 4-channel cable.

Tumble (20 HP)

Five rhythm cores ("rolz"). Each charges, flips its gate, charges again. A TOUCH knob sits between each pair of neighbours, in a ring (5 touches 1). Right pulls the two together so they fall into step; left pushes them apart so they lurch and stumble. Every time a rolz gate goes high it strikes its own gong.

ControlWhat it does
RATE 1 to 50.25 to 20 Hz each, before TEMPO. The light flashes on each strike.
TOUCH 1↔2 ... 5↔1Coupling between neighbours. A little jitter is added like a real finger.
TOUCH CVAdds to the knob (10 V = full right). Patch a gate from a sequencer or a MIDI key: it acts like a finger pressing the plates.
GATE 1 to 5Each rolz as a 0/10 V gate. Use them to fire your drums.
TEMPO + CVAll five faster or slower (÷4 to ×4; CV 1 V = double).
SYNCRestarts all five together and strikes all gongs. One pulse per bar keeps the rolls loopable.
PITCH, SPREAD, TONE, DECAYGong pitch for rolz 1 (40 Hz to 1.3 kHz, V/OCT in); each next rolz SPREAD semitones higher; WOOD to METAL; 30 ms to 3 s.
OUT L / RThe five gongs panned left to right.

Patches to start with

Breathing LFO (Swerve). RANGE CV, UP and DOWN at noon. Patch a slow Gallop horse into HIGH. As HIGH drops, the LFO gets faster and smaller. Send TRI to a filter cutoff in your techno loop.
Envelope with bend (Swerve). MODE ONCE, RANGE CV, UP fast, DOWN slow. Kick gate into ▲ TRIG, TRI to a VCA. Patch an LFO to LOW and the tail ends at a moving floor.
Fourses drone (Gallop). RANGE AUDIO, rates near each other, RAIL 5 V. Listen to MIX through a reverb. Turn one TILT slowly and the other three follow. Push RATE 2 far up to hear paradox fizz.
Self-mutating modulation (Gallop). RANGE CV. POLY into a Mixxa or into four filter cutoffs. Nothing repeats exactly, which is the Autechre-style movement without random.
Rolling percussion (Tumble). Clock ÷16 into SYNC. TOUCH 1↔2 right, 3↔4 left. GATE 1 to a kick, GATE 3 to hats, OUT L/R to the mixer. Patch a sequencer gate to TOUCH CV 2↔3 for fills that pull two rolz together for a beat.
Tuned gongs. Tumble PITCH from your chord root (V/OCT), SPREAD 7 (fifths) or 5 (fourths), TONE low, DECAY long: a slowly tumbling melodic bed.

Notes

Our own designs and names, inspired by Peter Blasser (Ciat-Lonbarde / Mobenthey) horse and rolz circuits; no schematics or artwork were copied. Untested in Rack yet. Source: hardyfinn/2026SoloModules, folder Paddock.
